blockers.summary: issue #205 requires native 32.768 microsecond DSA-110 resolution; the preparation code delivers 65.5 microseconds and offers no knob
blockers.evidence: [zach] AUTO-TF DSA  : 24 ch x 7.8 MHz, dt=65.5 us (f256/t2); window 23.8 ms; peak S/N 38/px
blockers.mechanism: band reconciliation, not the per-band resolution choice. choose_resolution returns t_factor 1 (native 32.768 us) for DSA-110 from its own 41-sample on-pulse window. _common_peak_relative_window then unions the two bands' windows in peak-relative time; CHIME/FRB's own window is 9280 native CHIME samples, so the union spans 23.8 ms = 726 native DSA-110 samples. _build_model (joint_tf_prep.py:439-442) re-applies the MAX_TIME_BINS cap to that reconciled window: 726 // 1 > 512, so the decimation doubles to 2 and DSA-110 lands at 65.5 us.
blockers.mechanism_verified_by: oracle re-derivation on the real Zach probes: cap 512 -> t_factor 2 (65.5 us); cap 1024 -> t_factor 1 (32.8 us)
blockers.mechanism_correction: an earlier draft of this receipt attributed the decimation to a floor inside choose_resolution. That was wrong: choose_resolution's floor for this band is 1. The cap that fires is the one in _build_model, acting on the reconciled common window. The practical difference matters: the DSA-110 band is coarsened because CHIME/FRB's window is long, not because DSA-110 needs it.
blockers.config_override_note: t_factor: 1 in the band configuration cannot help, because the cap runs after the per-band resolution choice
resolution_options: raise MAX_TIME_BINS to at least 1024 for this experiment (roughly doubles the DSA-110 sample count in the joint likelihood, and the sampler cost with it)
blockers.owner_relevance: this is the resolution family that produced the earlier collapsed C2D4 result at coarse binning
